thread:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Declared **SEV2** - Elevated request timeouts / 5xx in Hosted us-east. Suspected TP workers stuck (multi-GPU). Owner: @Sean Gallagher. Auto-links: dashboard https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/runtime-hosted-overview?var=region=us-east | runbook https://runbooks.redwood.ai/runtime/tp-hang

Sean Gallagher: I’m IC. Rafael on comms/ops? Need quick read on impact + mitigation options.

Rafael Mendes: On it. Seeing timeouts spike starting ~6 min ago. p95 latency for `chat.completions` up ~4x. 5xx at ~3.1% in us-east hosted pool `gpu-a100-80g-tp8`. Retries amplifying.

Omar El-Sayed: Pulling a few example traces now. Pattern looks like long streams that stop making forward progress; no GPU OOM. Correlates with `tp_group_id` repeating across failures.

Dev Patel: Support pinged: 2 tickets coming in (Dedicated + one big hosted customer) reporting “stream hung / never completes”. No data loss but customer app threads stuck.

Sean Gallagher: Immediate goals: stop bleeding (reduce customer-visible timeouts) + preserve capacity. Mitigations: shift traffic, drain stuck workers, temporarily reduce TP usage.

Rafael Mendes: Agree. We can traffic-shift some % from us-east -> us-west for Hosted. Dedicated impacted? I only see Hosted so far.

Dev Patel: Dedicated account in eu-west says intermittent, but today’s spike seems Hosted us-east. I’ll keep triage separate.

Sean Gallagher: Let’s do hosted mitigation first.
- Action 1: shift 30% to us-west (if SLO allows)
- Action 2: drain + restart nodes in the worst pool
- Action 3: flip config to reduce TP concurrency / disable long streaming on TP pool?

Connor O'Brien: For config changes, we can do a runtime flag hot-reload on hosted pool (no full deploy) but it’s a bit risky. Restarting nodes is safest.

Rafael Mendes: I can do traffic shift now. Any constraints? Some customers pinned to us-east for data residency.

Sean Gallagher: Shift only non-pinned. Keep pinned in-region.

DeployBot: Traffic Manager: starting weighted shift for Hosted `chat` routes: us-east 70% -> 40%, us-west 30% -> 60% (excluding residency-pinned tenants). ChangeID=tm-88421

Rafael Mendes: Drain plan: identify top offenders by watchdog-less stall signature. Omar, can you give hostnames / tp_group_ids?

Omar El-Sayed: Yup. From logs: `tp_group_id=tp-7f3c` on `hosted-use1-a100-12` + `hosted-use1-a100-19` repeatedly. Kernel time flat, NCCL calls never return. One trace shows `CollectiveAllReduce` span > 900s.

Hiro Tanaka: This smells like NCCL async error not surfacing + collectives stuck. We’ve seen similar in staging with streaming cancels. Not surprised it wedges a full TP group.

Sofia Ivanova: Scheduler side: if one rank is wedged, the group stays “available” and keeps getting work (no quarantine) -> amplifies. We need to stop scheduling onto that group once we detect no forward progress. For now, only mitigation is restart / cordon.

Sean Gallagher: Ok. Cordoning those hosts from scheduler / draining pool is next.

Rafael Mendes: I’ll cordon `hosted-use1-a100-12` + `-19` and rotate replacement capacity.

DeployBot: Cluster Manager: cordon requested for nodes [hosted-use1-a100-12, hosted-use1-a100-19]. Evicting active runtime pods with grace=30s. JobID=cm-55309

Dev Patel: Can we share customer-facing note for support? “We’re mitigating; rerouting traffic; if you see hangs, retry with shorter max_tokens / disable streaming temporarily”? Need consistent guidance.

Sean Gallagher: Keep it minimal until stabilized. Dev, tell support: “We’re investigating increased timeouts in us-east. Mitigation in progress. Workaround: retry requests; if streaming hangs, client should apply a per-request timeout and retry.” Don’t mention TP unless asked.

Dev Patel: Got it.

Omar El-Sayed: Post-traffic shift, 5xx is already trending down (now ~1.4%). p95 improving but still elevated vs baseline.

Rafael Mendes: Cordon complete. Pods draining. We should see TP groups reset once those hosts recycle.

Connor O'Brien: If this comes back, next lever is to temporarily reduce `max_inflight_per_tp_group` in hosted pool. That reduces likelihood of wedging under sustained load but will hurt throughput.

Sofia Ivanova: We can also raise cancellation aggressiveness? But honestly that’s part of the deadlock vector. I’d avoid touching that mid-incident.

Hiro Tanaka: Agreed. Also avoid enabling new NCCL flags live unless we’ve validated. Restart + traffic shift is safest.

Mateo Alvarez: Jumping in. Thanks for quick mitigation. Please capture: how quickly did we detect, what signals were missing (watchdog/quarantine). This is exactly the failure mode we’re targeting in the TP stability project.

Sean Gallagher: Will do. Current state?

Rafael Mendes: Metrics update:
- us-east 5xx down to 0.4% (baseline ~0.2%)
- timeouts down materially
- p95 latency still +25% but improving
- no new stuck tp_group_ids in last 10 min

Omar El-Sayed: Confirmed. The prior `tp_group_id=tp-7f3c` is gone after restart. No new collectives > 60s on the dashboard.

Sean Gallagher: Great. Let’s hold SEV2 until stable for 30 min.

Dev Patel: Support asks if Dedicated customers are impacted. I’ll answer “no confirmed Dedicated impact; monitoring.”

Rafael Mendes: One more thing: us-east pool autoscaler is still catching up after draining nodes; some queuing is expected.

Sean Gallagher: OK. Next steps / handoff:
1) Runtime to investigate root cause (NCCL stall + cancellation/barrier interplay).
2) SRE to add temporary alert: collective latency > N sec + no token progress per rank (if available).
3) Create incident summary + link logs.

Sofia Ivanova: We’ll open an ENG issue referencing this incident. Need log bundle + tp_group_id list + affected versions. Omar can you drop the runtime build hash?

Omar El-Sayed: Runtime build in us-east hosted: `runtime-1.18.7+build.4921`. Driver 535.129.03 (A100). I’ll attach log links in the runtime channel too.

Hiro Tanaka: Please also capture whether this happened with `streaming=true` + long context. That’s where we’ve seen barrier/cancel issues.

Omar El-Sayed: All examples were streaming, mixed seq lengths, high concurrency.

DeployBot: Cluster Manager: replacement nodes ready; pool `gpu-a100-80g-tp8` back to desired capacity. JobID=cm-55309 status=complete

Rafael Mendes: Looks stable now. 5xx at 0.22% last 5 min. Latency back near baseline.

Sean Gallagher: Marking SEV2 as mitigated, leaving thread open for follow-ups. Runtime team: please take handoff for RC and fix tracking. I’ll write incident notes + timeline.

Mateo Alvarez: Thanks. Sofia/Hiro: fold this into TP stability fixes workstream. We should treat “stuck group keeps receiving work” as a must-fix.

Sofia Ivanova: Ack. Will link to the scheduler quarantine work.

Rafael Mendes: I’ll file a quick internal action item for alerting and add the traffic-shift playbook snippet we used today.

Sean Gallagher: Closing oncall loop. :thumbsup:
